title: Thorn and Wolf
premise: Cyrus Zhou has spent years guarding the sealed Thornfell gate, content to be nobody—until a smuggler's stolen ledger reveals their name in the Prophecies of Ash, written a century before their birth. Hunted by the king's inquisitors and courted by the exiled wolf-clans of the other side, Cyrus learns they are the last heir of the gatekeepers who broke the covenant between realms. To reforge it, they must surrender either their hidden identity or the smuggler Wren Vale, who has become the only person who ever truly saw them. In the end, Cyrus chooses neither sacrifice offered: they bind the covenant to themselves as its living keeper, opening the gate to lawful passage and walking out of prophecy—and out of hiding—forever.
about_author: D. M. Oyelaran is the pen name of a former cartographer who once mapped smuggling routes through real mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, both the kind drawn on maps and the kind drawn around hearts.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Ash
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. During a routine interception of a smuggler named Wren Vale, Cyrus discovers a century-old prophetic ledger bearing their own name and tonight's date. The emotional beat is vertigo: a life built on invisibility collapses in a single page, and Cyrus must decide whether to arrest Wren or trust them.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Cyrus and Wren. Fleeing the king's inquisitors through forgotten gatekeeper tunnels, Cyrus uncovers their true heritage while Wren reveals the wolf-clans' starving exile. The beat is reluctant intimacy: two people with every reason to betray each other begin choosing honesty instead.

chapters.title: The Price of the Covenant
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, then shared. At the ruined covenant-stone, an inquisitor ambush forces the prophecy's cruel terms into the open: the gate opens only for a keeper's blood or a keeper's love. The climax breaks Cyrus open—they offer their own life, and Wren refuses to let them die alone.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Open Road
chapters.summary: Shared POV resolving into Cyrus's voice. Refusing both sacrifices, Cyrus binds their living self to the covenant, making the gate a lawful crossing between realms. The resolution is quiet and earned: identity claimed, duty transformed, and love no longer something to choose against.
